messages:
jamie: FYI hitting a weird error with rerank after copying the cURL from the Console. Paste -> 400 invalid JSON. Thought it was my payload but works fine when I handcraft it.
 alex: ugh, can you paste the exact cURL you copied? OS?
 jamie: MacBook Pro, zsh. Copied from Console > "Copy cURL (Windows)" accidentally (facepalm). Here's what Console gave me: 
 ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" 
 -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
 -d \"{\n  \"inputs\": [\n    \"What restaurants are open?\",\n    \"Nearby coffee shops\"\n  ],\n  \"candidates\": [\n    \"Cafe Latte\",\n    \"The Diner\"\n  ]\n}\"\n```
 jamie: When I run that I get: `{\"error\": \"Invalid JSON payload\"}`
 sara: yep that's the classic double-quoting issue. Console's Windows cURL includes extra escaping which breaks on zsh/bash if you paste the whole thing.
 alex: quick repro: the `-d \"{...}\"` wrapper causes the shell to see literal backslashes and quotes differently. On mac/linux either remove the outer escaping or use single-quoted JSON: `-d '{\"inputs\": [...]}'`
 jamie: interesting — but even after fixing quotes the reranker returns weird scores (all 0.0 or same score). Could that be related?
 kyle: possible. Two things: 1) malformed input arrays (e.g., an inputs string with embedded newline chars) can be coerced into single string candidate, hitting the per-item length limit and causing truncated/degenerate scores. 2) If server receives single string instead of array, rerank assumes single query and returns default tie scores.
 jamie: i did have multiline entries copied from a doc (newlines between bullets). When I replaced newlines with `\n` it worked and scores looked reasonable.
 alex: handy minimal fixes: 
 - Use Console's "Copy JSON payload" if available. 
 - On mac/linux: `curl -X POST ... -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"inputs\": [\"a\",\"b\"] , \"candidates\": [\"x\",\"y\"]}'`
 - On Windows (cmd.exe) use `^` line continuations or use PowerShell's `-Body` param with `Invoke-RestMethod`.
 jamie: is this a docs bug? Console shouldn't offer the Windows cURL as the default for mac users.
 docs-bot: created docs issue RDW-2389: Console cURL copy selects platform-specific escaping inconsistently. Assigned to eng-docs.
 sara: also adding a tiny runtime validation check — if `inputs` is a string, return a helpful 400: "expected array of strings for inputs" instead of generic parse error. Filing RDW-2390.
 alex: rn quick workaround: pipe a file to curl to avoid shell escaping: `curl -X POST ... -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @payload.json` where payload.json contains raw JSON (no extra escaping).
 jamie: tried `--data-binary @payload.json` and that fixed both the parse error and the odd scores. thanks!
 ops-bot: deploy scheduled for docs fix RDW-2389 at 2025-08-14T03:00Z (rolling).
 kyle: we'll also add a small note in the rerank console UI about platform-specific cURL quoting and multiline items.
 jamie: awesome — leaving this thread. tagging reproduction steps here for the ticket: 1) Console copy (Windows) pasted into zsh -> 400; 2) same payload file -> works; 3) multiline inputs preserved -> truncated scores; 4) `\n` or file upload -> good.
 alex: perfect, thanks for the clear repro. closing loop once docs live. :thumbsup:
